text:
ConocoPhillips edged up 0.23% today to $137.35, continuing a steady climb over the past two weeks (+6.05%). The gain reflects ongoing strength in oil prices driven by Middle East supply disruptions — Saudi Arabia shut down a critical pipeline bypass after attacks from Iran-aligned groups, and a vessel was struck in the Strait of Hormuz, a major chokepoint for global oil flows. US crude is trading at $97.26 per barrel, up sharply from earlier in the week, which directly supports earnings for oil producers like ConocoPhillips.

The stock's broader two-week rally sits atop conflicting signals about how long these disruptions will last. While Trump has suggested oil prices could fall sharply after midterm elections if Iran tensions ease, Iranian leadership is taking a harder line, and diplomatic talks remain uncertain. For now, elevated oil prices are the dominant driver — every dollar per barrel matters significantly to ConocoPhillips' profitability — but the durability of this rally depends on whether Middle East tensions escalate or de-escalate in coming weeks.
